catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.home.v1 is the closest class, but its optional axes and speed_scale inputs have no counterpart in this binding: FlexMotionController.home() with no axes is a full home, and the controller exposes no speed argument for it. The skeleton-schema expansion would publish those inputs while the driver refuses them, so the exact input-free full-home operation is an extension.
catalogue_requests.summary: Home every Flex axis (a full home, which also clears the halt recovery gate).

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.stop.v1 declares an optional deceleration profile, but FlexMotionController.stop() takes no argument and runs the OT3API halt path. Binding the class would publish a deceleration input the driver cannot apply. The extension is the exact input-free halt and is the declared safe-state action.
catalogue_requests.summary: Halt all Flex motion through the native stop (also the declared safe state).

ENTRY AND SHAPE: the card lists three override-confirmed entry symbols. This package binds the first, unitelabs.opentrons_flex.io.flex_motion:FlexMotionController (flex_motion.py:99), the shared OT3 motion controller; the HeaterShakerController and ThermocyclerController are separate module devices and are NOT COVERED (one package serves one device). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver, but the native interface is asynchronous, takes OT3Mount and opentrons.types.Point, and returns the class output schemas; a direct Driver with native.py is used, matching the card's own decision 'direct-driver'. native.py is the production adapter: it builds FlexMotionController.build(simulate=False) and converts the driver's plain mount name and [x, y, z] list to OT3Mount and Point; the fake implements the same adapter contract. The driver never imports the Opentrons stack at gate time.

COVERAGE: reads simulating (is_simulating), lights_button, lights_rails (get_lights) and machine_status (E-stop, door, error flag); writes lights_button and lights_rails through set_lights(button=..., rails=...) and reads them back; action cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 moves the LEFT pipette mount through move_to(mount, point) - the catalogue class has no mount field, so the binding is the LEFT mount and native.py also accepts right/gripper; extension home_all calls home() (full home); extension halt_motion calls stop() and is the safe-state action. The two extension ids are listed in catalogue_requests.

LIMITS: no text file of the clone states the deck workspace of a configured Flex; position.x, position.y and position.z are Limit.operator_required, so a move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies the envelope. site-limits.example.json is example operator data only (0..400 mm, not a device fact); fixtures/conformance.json supplies in-range, alternate and out-of-envelope positions because the class example 300/0/250 does not fit the example overlay. No G4 warnings were reported.

SAFETY: risk is R2 from the card floor and from the robot-arm/pipetting hazard (MHS/spec/04-safety.md). The independent hardware stop is the Flex E-stop cited at docs/flex_system_acceptance.md:58 (estop_physical_ref); the native @estop calls FlexMotionController.stop(), the OT3API halt path (flex_motion.py:291-305), and the input-free safe-state action does the same (a second idempotent halt). The halt is not the physical E-stop and does not claim to be safety-rated. It leaves the robot recovery-gated (recovery_state.py:47-54), so this package declares no estop_terminal and no re-enable: an operator reset releases only the MHS latch, and the full-home extension is the first motion after it; no @reset hook bypasses the operator envelope. The runtime reads machine_status before and after commands, but the driver cannot sense physical quiescence beyond the upstream halt acknowledgement.

For the human reviewer: Opentrons Flex gantry, R2 (motion only; pipetting, gripper and modules NOT COVERED). The stop halts motion in progress at the connector (it cancels the running operation, whose cancel path halts too) and is acknowledged by the awaited OT3API halt(), not confirmed by a sensed state: what halt() sends on the CAN bus and whether the motors stay energised or hold the Z axes afterwards is Opentrons 8.8.1 code outside the clone, so confirm it on the robot with the Flex E-stop in reach. One e-stop can send the halt several times (estop method, safe-state action, cancellation-to-safe-state, CORE-086 second run); each only marks the robot halted again. After any halt, cancellation or deadline expiry the robot needs the full home (the re-enable), which moves every axis: clear the deck and give it a long enough deadline (30 s default). native.py builds its own OT3API on the CAN bus: stop the sila2-connector and opentrons-robot-server services first (README.md:16-20, 32-33) and run it on the Flex under Python 3.10 with opentrons 8.8.1. The deck envelope is operator_required (the example overlay is not device data); the move uses the LEFT mount at the OT3API default speed. The clone states no licence.
